headline: French Lunch Foundation 10
threshold: Greet, ask, order and clarify a simple lunch in French with English support.

lessons.title: Lunch Greetings and French Sounds
lessons.objective: Greet lunch staff politely, introduce yourself, and say common lunch words clearly in French.
lessons.focus: Use bonjour and vous with an unfamiliar server. Hear é in café, French u in jus, the nasal vowel in pain, and the silent final t in poulet.

words.note: In a restaurant, la carte lists dishes; un menu can mean a set meal.

lessons.speaking: Greet the server with vous, say your name, ask for the menu, and pronounce café, jus, pain, and poulet.

speakingScene.goal: Greet the server with vous, say your name, ask for the menu, and pronounce café, jus, pain, and poulet.

lessons.title: People, Portions, Euros and Time
lessons.objective: Give a group size, order counted lunch items, confirm a price in euros, and state an arrival time.
lessons.focus: Count from zéro through dix, cent and mille. Use nous sommes for group size, deux menus for counted items, un verre d'eau for quantity, and à midi et demi for 12:30. Euro amounts use euros after the number.

words.en: Does that come to twenty-five euros?

lessons.speaking: Say there are four of you, order two set meals and three sandwiches, give the 12:30 arrival time, and confirm the euro total.

lessons.title: Describe Food and Find a Table
lessons.objective: Ask whether a table is free, describe a dish's taste and temperature, and locate a nearby place.
lessons.focus: French uses être for both description and current condition: la soupe est chaude, la sauce est épicée. Use il y a for availability and se trouve or est for location; Spanish ser/estar is source context, not a French verb contrast.

words.en: The market is very close by.

lessons.speaking: Ask whether a table is free and whether the sauce is spicy; describe the soup's temperature and taste; ask where the market is.

speakingScene.goal: Ask whether a table is free and whether the sauce is spicy; describe the soup's temperature and taste; ask where the market is.

reader.en: Yes, it is free. The other table is taken.

reader.fr: La sauce est épicée ?
reader.en: Is the sauce spicy?

reader.speaker: Server

reader.speaker: Sam

reader.en: I'll have the soup. It's delicious!

reader.speaker: Server
reader.fr: Vous cherchez autre chose ?
reader.en: Are you looking for anything else?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.fr: Oui. Le marché est loin ?
reader.en: Yes. Is the market far?

reader.speaker: Server
reader.fr: Non, le marché est tout près. Il est ouvert.
reader.en: No, the market is very close by. It is open.

lessons.title: What Is Available for Lunch
lessons.objective: Ask what the restaurant has today, say what you want or need, and request a utensil.
lessons.focus: Use il y a for availability, avoir for what someone has, je voudrais for a polite wish, and il faut for what must be done.

lessons.speaking: Ask whether there is a set lunch, say you want the soup, and request a spoon and a napkin.

lessons.title: Going to Lunch and Asking Permission
lessons.objective: Say where you are going to eat, what you plan to order, and whether you can pay by card.
lessons.focus: Use aller à for destinations, aller + infinitive for a plan, faire for what a place makes, and pouvoir for permission.

words.es: Je vais au marché pour manger.
words.en: I am going to the market to eat.
We are going to have lunch at the bistro.

lessons.speaking: Tell your companion where you are going, then ask the server whether you can sit and pay by card.

lessons.title: What We Eat, Share and Pay
lessons.objective: Describe what you and others eat, share, prepare and pay for in the French present tense.
lessons.focus: Compare je mange, tu manges, vous mangez, nous partageons, ils vendent and je paie. French present forms follow French verb groups rather than Spanish -ar/-er/-ir endings.

words.es: Je mange des haricots avec du riz.

lessons.speaking: Tell your companion what you eat, ask whether they eat avocado, say what you share and how you pay.

lessons.title: Questions About the Daily Special
lessons.objective: Ask what a dish includes, where things are, its price, and which dish the server recommends.
lessons.focus: Use qu’est-ce que/que, qui, où, quand, combien, comment, pourquoi and lequel/laquelle in direct lunch questions.

lessons.title: No, Never and Another Serving
lessons.objective: Say what you do not eat, request more or less, and decline another offer politely.
lessons.focus: Use ne…pas, ne…jamais, ne…rien and personne in full sentences; use pas encore, plus, moins, encore and sans with food.

words.es: Je ne mange pas de porc.

lessons.title: Polite Requests at the Table
lessons.objective: Ask for ice, takeaway packaging, separate bills and the check using polite French requests.
lessons.focus: Use pourriez-vous and s’il vous plaît to request service. Contrast l’addition (the bill) with la monnaie (change).

words.en: Could you bring us the bill, please?

words.es: Un verre avec des glaçons, s’il vous plaît.

words.en: Could you pack that to go?

lessons.speaking: Ask for a glass with ice, a takeaway bag, and separate bills; then request the bill and say to keep the change.

lessons.title: Menu Cognates and Asking for Help
lessons.objective: Recognize useful French menu cognates and ask for repetition, slower speech and a vegetarian option.
lessons.focus: Notice French -tion, -té and -ent in réservation, spécialité and ingrédient. Use je ne comprends pas, pouvez-vous répéter and plus lentement to repair comprehension.
